summary: One skill: the catalog's index is generated from its chapters, each chapter read on demand.

skills.description: Generic software-architecture and engineering standards: styles (modular monolith, hexagonal, event-driven...), principles (SOLID, single source of truth), patterns and anti-patterns, ISO/IEC 25010 quality attributes, C4/ADR, API/data/testing/delivery, security (OWASP, STRIDE), operations, and the AI/agentic layer (MCP, A2A, skills, evals). Use when making or reviewing an architecture or design decision, choosing a pattern, designing an API or schema, or planning a refactor.

chapters.title: 1. Architecture styles
chapters.summary: deployment topology, internal structure, communication, data, integration, UI and hosting -- orthogonal axes real systems combine

chapters.title: 2. Design principles
chapters.summary: SOLID, GRASP, single source of truth and the named laws engineers cite

chapters.title: 3. Design patterns and anti-patterns
chapters.summary: GoF, enterprise, integration, distributed, resilience and concurrency patterns, and the anti-patterns to refuse

chapters.title: 4. Quality attributes (ISO/IEC 25010)
chapters.summary: the attributes an architecture trades -- name the one gained and the one lost

chapters.title: 5. Documentation and modeling
chapters.summary: C4, arc42, ADRs, fitness functions, benchmark sources

chapters.title: 6. Formal standards and methods
chapters.summary: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010, DDD, 12-factor, Well-Architected, ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF

chapters.title: 7. API, data, testing, security and delivery
chapters.summary: API contracts and errors, data consistency, the test pyramid, delivery and accessibility

chapters.title: 8. AI-system and agentic layer
chapters.summary: RAG pipelines, MCP, A2A, Agent Skills, context engineering, evals and GenAI observability

chapters.title: 9. Security
chapters.summary: OWASP, ASVS, STRIDE, zero trust, supply-chain provenance and the LLM/agentic threat lists

chapters.title: 10. Operations and reliability
chapters.summary: observability, SLOs, scaling, caching, trunk-based delivery, IaC and GitOps

chapters.title: 11. Craftsmanship and refactoring
chapters.summary: code smells, the refactoring catalog, the bar for done, debugging discipline

chapters.title: 12. Declarative and config-driven platforms
chapters.summary: config as source of truth, interpreter plus registry, schema-driven contracts, safe expressions

chapters.title: 13. Verdict method
chapters.summary: judging a design: invariants binary, criteria evidence-bound, attributes by a written decision hierarchy
